study: Borman et al. 2007 (Success for All national RCT, Year-3 reading, AERJ 44(3))
eval_evidence: Co-authored by the SFA developers / Success for All Foundation affiliates (Slavin, Madden, Chamberlain, Chambers); Slavin and Madden are the program developers. Per codebook, developer co-authorship => 'developer' (despite the IES grant and lead academic Borman).
developer_evidence: Training and ongoing support delivered by 'Trainers from the Success for All Foundation' (the developer organization): 3 days initial training, ~16 days first-year on-site support, ~15 days/year thereafter, quarterly implementation visits; trainers visited classrooms.
cascade_evidence: Success for All Foundation (developer) trainers train and support the school staff/teachers directly, plus a full-time on-site program facilitator; no external trained-trainer tier.
counterfactual_evidence: Control = business-as-usual; control schools could purchase/implement any innovation other than Success for All (no active alternative imposed).
coaching_evidence: Full-time on-site program facilitator overseeing daily operation, ~16 days first-year on-site support, ~15 days/year ongoing PD, quarterly SFAF fidelity/implementation visits with trainers visiting classrooms -- recurring on-site, in-class support.
student_dose_evidence: SFA includes one-to-one tutoring for struggling readers in grades 1-3 by specially trained certified teachers/paraprofessionals -- a direct student-facing dose beyond regular instruction (designed component; the paper notes few schools fully implemented it).
maturity_evidence: Outcomes are the Year-3 (spring grade 2) wave; schools had implemented SFA for ~3 years (>=1 prior implementation year), so the program/teachers are past their first implementation year.
